# RevenueDot

> RevenueDot is an open-source backend for in-app purchases and subscriptions that works with the RevenueCat SDK. Start free on RevenueDot Cloud (https://app.revenuedot.app/signup, free up to $10,000 monthly tracked revenue) or self-host it. An app points the RevenueCat SDK's proxy URL at RevenueDot and keeps its purchase code, offerings and customers.

It verifies App Store and Google Play purchases on the server, keeps each customer's entitlements current from store notifications, and sends webhooks in RevenueCat's payload format. On RevenueDot Cloud, apps use the API at https://api.revenuedot.app and people sign in to the dashboard at https://app.revenuedot.app/login. Self-hosted, RevenueDot runs as one Docker image plus Postgres. The server is AGPL-3.0. The SDK forks are MIT and keep RevenueCat's class and method names. RevenueDot is not affiliated with RevenueCat, Inc.

Every link below is the page's Markdown. Full text: [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms-full.txt) (everything), or one file per section under [llms/](https://github.com/revenuedot/docs/blob/main/llms).

## Getting started

- [Getting started: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/getting-started.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [What is RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/getting-started/README.md): RevenueDot is an open-source backend for in-app purchases and subscriptions that works with the RevenueCat SDK. Start free on RevenueDot Cloud or self-host it, point the SDK's proxy URL at it and keep your app code.
- [How do I make a first purchase with RevenueDot in 5 minutes?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Create a free RevenueDot Cloud account, add a Test Store app with a product and an entitlement, make a test purchase from the dashboard, then point the RevenueCat SDK at https://api.revenuedot.app. You can also run the same server yourself with Docker.
- [How do I connect my app to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/getting-started/connect-your-app.md): Three ways. Proxy mode sets one URL in the RevenueCat SDK you already ship. The RevenueDot fork swaps the package. The importer keeps your existing RevenueCat API keys working.

## Concepts

- [Concepts: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/concepts.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [How is RevenueDot organized?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/README.md): A server holds projects. A project holds apps (one per store), a catalog of products, entitlements, offerings and packages, and customers with their purchases and events.
- [What are projects, apps and API keys?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/projects-and-apps.md): A project is one product you sell. An app is that product on one store, with its own public SDK key. Secret keys belong to a project and unlock the REST API.
- [How do products and entitlements work?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/products-and-entitlements.md): A product is one item on one store. An entitlement is the access your app checks, such as pro. Attach every product that should unlock it; the app then checks the entitlement, never a product id.
- [How do offerings and packages decide what my paywall shows?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/offerings-and-packages.md): An offering is a set of packages, and each package holds one product per app. The SDK shows the current offering, so you change the paywall's products on the server without an app update.
- [How do customers, app user IDs and logIn work?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/customers-and-app-user-ids.md): A customer is one person with one or more app user IDs. The SDK starts with an anonymous ID; logIn attaches your own ID; the project's transfer behaviour decides who owns a restored purchase.
- [How does RevenueDot track a subscription's lifecycle and which events does it send?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/subscriptions-and-events.md): RevenueDot keeps one record per subscription, updates it from receipts and store notifications, compares the old and new state, and records RevenueCat-style events such as RENEWAL and EXPIRATION.
- [How does RevenueDot keep sandbox purchases apart from real ones?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/concepts/sandbox.md): Every purchase carries an environment, sandbox or production, taken from the store. Metrics count production by default, and each webhook can receive one environment or both.

## SDK guides

- [SDK guides: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/sdks.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [Which RevenueCat SDKs work with RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/README.md): All nine RevenueCat app SDKs work with RevenueDot in proxy mode today. Set the proxy URL and turn off signature checks. RevenueDot forks of all of them are released.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with the iOS SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/ios.md): Set Purchases.proxyURL before configure and turn entitlement verification off. The RevenueCat iOS SDK 5.x then talks to your RevenueDot server with no other code change.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with the Android SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/android.md): Set Purchases.proxyURL before configure and set EntitlementVerificationMode.DISABLED. The stock SDK still sends diagnostics, paywall and ad events to RevenueCat; the fork fixes that.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with React Native and Expo?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/react-native.md): Await Purchases.setProxyURL before configure. Verification is already off by default in react-native-purchases, and Expo Go and web work with a Test Store key.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with Flutter?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/flutter.md): Await Purchases.setProxyURL before configure on iOS and Android. Flutter web ignores the proxy URL in the stock purchases_flutter package; the RevenueDot fork fixes it.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with the web SDK (purchases-js)?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/web.md): Pass httpConfig.proxyURL to Purchases.configure and turn off analytics events. purchases-js buys with Test Store (test_) keys; to take real payments on the web, send buyers to a RevenueDot purchase link or funnel on your Stripe account.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with Capacitor and Ionic?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/capacitor.md): Await Purchases.setProxyURL({ url }) before configure, and pass entitlementVerificationMode DISABLED, because the Capacitor plugin passes no default and the native informational default applies.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with Kotlin Multiplatform?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/kotlin-multiplatform.md): Set Purchases.proxyURL, a String, before Purchases.configure in common code. purchases-kmp already defaults to EntitlementVerificationMode.DISABLED, so nothing else changes.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with Unity?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/unity.md): Fill in the Proxy URL field on the Purchases component and set Entitlement Verification Mode to Disabled in the Inspector. Unity has no public SetProxyURL method.
- [How do I use RevenueDot with Cordova?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/cordova.md): Call Purchases.setProxyURL before configureWith. Cordova has no option to turn off signature checks, so it logs a verification failure for every response and still grants access.
- [What is purchases-hybrid-common, and do I need to install it?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/sdks/hybrid-common.md): purchases-hybrid-common is the shared native and TypeScript layer under the React Native, Flutter, Capacitor, Unity and Cordova SDKs. App developers never install it directly; the wrapper pulls it in.

## Guides: stores, web billing, webhooks, integrations, self-hosting

- [Guides: stores, web billing, webhooks, integrations, self-hosting: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/guides.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [Which guide do I need?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/README.md): Step-by-step guides for stores, web billing, webhooks, integrations, ads, attribution, benchmarks, growth insights, refunds, retention, support, testing, your team, Auth, moving, billing, Enterprise and its SLA, self-hosting and high availability.
- [How do I connect the App Store to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/app-store.md): Create an App Store app with your bundle ID, add an In-App Purchase key (.p8, key ID, issuer ID), then set RevenueDot's notification URL as the Server Notifications v2 URL in App Store Connect.
- [How do I connect Google Play to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/google-play.md): Create a Google Play app with your package name, upload a Google Cloud service account key with Play Console access, then push real-time developer notifications to RevenueDot through Pub/Sub.
- [How do I connect the Amazon Appstore to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/amazon-appstore.md): Create an Amazon app with your package name, save the Amazon shared key so RevenueDot can check receipts with Amazon's Receipt Verification Service, and add RevenueDot's URL as a Real-time Notifications endpoint.
- [How do I track Paddle Billing purchases in RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/paddle.md): Create a Paddle app with your Paddle API key, let RevenueDot add its notification destination in Paddle, import your prices, and post each Paddle subscription or transaction from your backend so the same entitlements unlock in your apps.
- [How do I connect a Roku channel to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/roku.md): Create a Roku app with your Roku Pay API key and channel ID, point RevenueCat's Roku SDK at RevenueDot, and set RevenueDot's URL as the Roku Pay push notification URL so renewals, failed payments, cancellations and refunds arrive.
- [How do I connect the Samsung Galaxy Store to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/galaxy-store.md): Create a Galaxy Store app with your package name and a Seller Portal service account, build your Android app with the RevenueCat SDK's Galaxy module pointed at RevenueDot, and set RevenueDot's URL for Samsung's server notifications.
- [How do I track Stripe subscriptions from my own Stripe account in RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/stripe.md): Create a Stripe app, save a restricted API key and a webhook signing secret from your own Stripe account, post each new subscription or Checkout Session to /v1/receipts, and let Stripe's webhooks keep it current.
- [How do I import my products from App Store Connect, Google Play or Stripe?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/import-products.md): Click Import products, pick the store products you already set up, and RevenueDot creates them in the catalog with their type, duration and name, attached to the entitlements you choose. Works with App Store Connect, Google Play and Stripe; Amazon products are added by SKU.
- [How do I change App Store and Google Play prices with the product editor?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/product-editor.md): Download a CSV of your App Store or Google Play products with a price per territory, change prices or add products, upload it, review every change, and commit it to the store. The Products page shows each product's store price and status.
- [How do I sell my app's subscriptions on the web with Stripe?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/web-billing.md): Connect your Stripe account with a restricted key and a webhook, add a web config, let RevenueDot create web products in Stripe, put them in an offering, then share a purchase link or publish a funnel. Buyers pay on Stripe Checkout and unlock the app with a redemption link.
- [How do I share a checkout link for an offering?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/purchase-links.md): A purchase link is a hosted checkout page for one offering at /pay/<project>/<link>. Add ?app_user_id= to buy for a signed-in user, ?email= to pre-fill the email and ?code= to pre-fill a discount code. Links can expire and carry an automatic discount.
- [How do I build a web-to-app funnel?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/funnels.md): Build a multi-step funnel (questions, info, email, paywall, success) in the dashboard or with AI, publish it to a public URL, sell on Stripe Checkout, and see where visitors drop off. Funnel events can go to webhooks, analytics tools and ad networks.
- [How does a web purchase reach my app?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/redemption-links.md): An anonymous web buyer gets a redemption link, <scheme>://redeem_web_purchase?redemption_token=…. Register the scheme, pass the link to redeemWebPurchase, and the purchase moves to the app's user. The results are success, invalidToken, purchaseBelongsToOtherUser and expired.
- [How do I give discounts at web checkout?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/web-discounts.md): Web discounts use RevenueCat's v2 discount fields and operations. Each discount is a Stripe coupon and each code a Stripe promotion code in your own account. Checkout checks that it is enabled, not expired, under its cap, for the plan, and that the buyer is eligible.
- [Where do my purchase links and funnels live, and can I use my own domain?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/custom-domains.md): Hosted pages live at <pay base>/<project slug>/<page>, which is https://api.revenuedot.app/pay on Cloud and your server's /pay (or REVENUEDOT_PAY_URL) when self-hosted. A custom domain needs a CNAME, a TXT record and Verify; on Cloud, TLS is then added by hand.
- [How do I receive and verify RevenueDot webhooks?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/webhooks.md): Add a webhook URL, keep the whsec_ signing secret, verify the X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature HMAC on the raw body, answer 200 fast and deduplicate on event.id. Failed deliveries retry 5 times.
- [How do Trusted Entitlements (response signing) work with RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/trusted-entitlements.md): With REVENUEDOT_SIGNING_KEY set, RevenueDot signs every SDK response the way the RevenueCat SDKs verify. The stock SDK trusts only RevenueCat's key, so turn verification off or use a fork built with your key.
- [How do I use the Test Store to test purchases without a store account?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/test-store.md): Add a Test Store app, use its test_ key in the SDK, and buy through the SDK's test dialog. Simulate renewals, cancellations, billing issues and refunds with POST /v2/projects/{id}/test_purchases.
- [How do I test with App Store sandbox, StoreKit in Xcode and Google Play testers?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/sandbox-testing.md): Real store test purchases work against RevenueDot once the app's store credentials and notifications are set up. They are marked sandbox; Xcode StoreKit purchases also need the StoreKit test certificate.
- [How do I self-host RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/self-hosting.md): Run the published image ghcr.io/revenuedot/revenuedot (API plus dashboard) next to Postgres with docker compose. Configure it with a .env file, put HTTPS in front, and set REVENUEDOT_SIGNING_KEY if you sign responses.
- [How do I run RevenueDot with high availability?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/high-availability.md): Run two or more replicas of the RevenueDot image behind a load balancer on one Postgres with a standby. Migrations and background work run once under Postgres locks. Helm chart, Terraform for AWS and Google Cloud.
- [How do I upgrade a self-hosted RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/upgrades.md): Back up the database, pull the new image and restart. The server applies new database migrations by itself when it starts; there is no separate migrate step.
- [How do I back up and restore a self-hosted RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/backups.md): Everything lives in Postgres. Back it up with pg_dump on a schedule, keep copies off the server, and restore with pg_restore while the RevenueDot container is stopped.
- [How do I move a project between self-hosted RevenueDot and RevenueDot Cloud, or export everything?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/move-projects.md): One command or the dashboard copies a project to another RevenueDot server with its ids, SDK keys, secret keys and webhook signing secrets, verifies every table, then forwards the old server's traffic. A full export gives you every table as JSON Lines with a manifest and checksums.
- [How does RevenueDot Cloud billing work?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/cloud-billing.md): RevenueDot Cloud is free up to $10,000 of tracked revenue a month. Cloud Standard costs 0.5% of the tracked revenue above $10,000, never more than $999 a month. Self-hosting is free and unmetered. See your usage, upgrade and manage your card on the Billing page.
- [What should I check before running RevenueDot in production?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/going-to-production.md): A checklist for a self-hosted RevenueDot with real customers - HTTPS, a real Postgres with backups, store credentials and notifications verified, webhooks tested, secrets kept out of apps, and monitoring.
- [How do I invite my team to a RevenueDot project?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/team.md): Project admins invite people by email with the Admin, Developer or Viewer role. The link lasts 7 days. Admins change roles and remove members; a project always keeps one admin.
- [How do I manage my RevenueDot account settings?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/account-settings.md): Change your email or password, turn on two-factor authentication, sign out sessions, revoke AI assistants, pick summary and anomaly emails, a theme, a tint, your first day of the week and the currency the dashboard shows.
- [Which alert emails does RevenueDot send?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/alerts.md): Project admins get an email when store notifications fail, a webhook fails 5 times in a row, an integration keeps failing, or Apple or Google rejects the store credentials. One email when it starts, at most one reminder a day, one when it is fixed.
- [Connect ChatGPT, Claude and other AI assistants](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/connect-ai-assistants.md): Connect RevenueDot to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor or Claude Code with OAuth, choose what the assistant may do, and run setup, support and health checks from chat.
- [How do I ask RevenueDot AI about my revenue and customers?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/revenuedot-ai.md): RevenueDot AI is the assistant in the dashboard. It answers from your own metrics, charts, customers and catalog, and changes things only after you approve each change. Admins choose read and write, read only, or off.
- [Paywalls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/paywalls.md): Build a native paywall from a template, with the visual editor or with AI, translate it, publish it to an offering, and show it in your app with RevenueCatUI's PaywallView.
- [Targeting and experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/targeting-and-experiments.md): Show different offerings to different customers with audiences and targeting rules on the Targeting page (Live, Scheduled, Inactive), set the default offering, use placements, and test offerings against each other with experiments.
- [How do I test offerings, prices, trials and paywalls with experiments?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md): An experiment shows each customer one of two to four offerings and reports which earns more, with 95% intervals and the chance to beat the control. Set up variants, enrollment, audience and priority, then read 18 metrics or export them as CSV.
- [Charts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/charts.md): Every built-in chart in RevenueDot, how each one is calculated, chart types, the customers behind each number, annotations, share links, the API, and the SQL that reproduces the core numbers.
- [How do I send purchase events to analytics, attribution and marketing tools, and export my data?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/integrations.md): Every entry of RevenueCat's integration catalogue (37) plus BigQuery. Connect a tool with its key, and every purchase, trial, renewal and refund is sent with RevenueCat's event names, retried and logged. Exports write CSV or Parquet to S3, R2 or GCS.
- [Ads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/ads.md): Ad revenue from the RevenueCat SDK's ad events in US dollars next to subscription revenue, with eCPM and breakdowns. Rewarded ads verified on the server with AdMob's signed callback, granting currency or access by rules. Optional AdMob connection.
- [How do win-back offers work with RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/win-back-offers.md): Apple's iOS 18 win-back offers work with the RevenueCat SDK and RevenueDot unchanged. RevenueDot records the offer on each purchase, sends it as offer_code in webhooks and exports it, and keeps Apple's list of offers a lapsed customer may redeem.
- [What happens to my customers' access when RevenueDot is down?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/offline-entitlements.md): The RevenueCat SDKs keep paying customers' access while the server answers 5xx, using a product-to-entitlement mapping RevenueDot serves for each app. How it works per store, and what to check.
- [How do I answer Apple refund requests with Refund Control?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/refund-control.md): Refund Control answers Apple's CONSUMPTION_REQUEST within 12 hours with consumption information and your refund preference, chosen by ordered policies on customer conditions. It also records Google Play refunds and chargebacks and shows refund rate, amounts and counts.
- [How do I show retention offers when customers cancel?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/retention.md): Offer a discount in the in-app Customer Center when a customer cancels or asks for a refund, and show a message, a cheaper plan or a promotional offer on Apple's own cancel screen with the Retention Messaging API.
- [How do I email churned subscribers a win-back offer?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/win-back-campaigns.md): Win-back campaigns email subscribers whose subscription ended a link back to the store, once per customer, with click tracking, optional open tracking, one-click unsubscribe and a count of customers who came back.
- [How do I handle support requests from the Customer Center?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/support-integrations.md): Customer Center tickets reach your support inbox with the customer's subscription details. RevenueDot's Intercom inbox app and Zendesk sidebar app show each customer's subscription, entitlements, total spent, refunds and open tickets next to the conversation.
- [How do I filter, save and export customer lists?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/customer-lists.md): The Customers page has built-in lists (all, active subscribers, sandbox, non-subscription, expired), saved audiences, filters from the audience condition builder, sortable columns, a hide-IDs switch, four summary cards and CSV export.
- [Which project settings does RevenueDot have?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/project-settings.md): Rename the project, limit who can test with sandbox purchases, hand ownership to another admin, keep brand colours and fonts for paywalls, block abusive app user IDs, and publish a public page of verified revenue numbers.
- [How do I sign users in with Firebase or OpenID Connect and link them to their purchases?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/auth.md): RevenueDot Auth (beta) checks your identity provider's ID token, signs the user in as their app user ID with logIn semantics, and returns a token your app uses to read customer info, attributes and in-app currency balances without a backend of its own.
- [Which RevenueDot plan has organizations, SSO and the other team features, and how do I turn them on?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/enterprise.md): Cloud Standard adds organizations, custom roles and single sign-on. Enterprise adds SCIM, audit retention, compliance exports, data location, the SLA and the licence for self-hosting. Self-hosted servers turn these features on with a licence key, as before.
- [What does the RevenueDot SLA promise?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/sla.md): RevenueDot Enterprise promises 99.9% monthly uptime for the purchase path on RevenueDot Cloud, with service credits, and support response times from 1 hour for failing purchases, on Cloud and self-hosted.
- [How do I set up single sign-on for RevenueDot with SAML or OpenID Connect?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/single-sign-on.md): Verify your email domain with a DNS TXT record, connect Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or any SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect provider, then optionally require SSO. Owners and contractors keep passwords.
- [How do I provision RevenueDot users and groups with SCIM?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/scim.md): Create a SCIM token, paste it and the base URL into Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, and map identity provider groups to project roles. Deactivating someone removes their access and ends their sessions at once.
- [Where is my RevenueDot data stored, and can I keep it in the EU?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/data-location.md): Self-hosted, your data stays wherever you run the server. Enterprise records a US or EU region on each organization and project; on Cloud each region is its own deployment that refuses other regions' projects. Cloud has no EU region yet.
- [How long does RevenueDot keep audit logs, and how do I export signed copies?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/audit-retention-and-exports.md): Owners set audit retention from 30 days to 10 years, or forever; an hourly job deletes older entries. Admins download the audit log and an access review as CSV or JSON, signed with Ed25519, up to 200,000 rows.
- [Attribution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/attribution.md): See which ad networks, campaigns, ad groups and keywords bring paying customers. RevenueDot stores the attribution the SDK already sends, names Apple Search Ads campaigns, segments every chart by it, and shows revenue by campaign with day-7, day-30 and to-date revenue and ROAS.
- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/benchmarks.md): Compare your trial conversion, churn, refund rate, LTV, ARPU and prices with similar apps on RevenueDot Cloud. Sharing is opt-in, groups need at least 10 apps, and no app, customer or exact count is ever shown.
- [How do I set up the Customer Center?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/customer-center.md): Pick the actions customers see on the in-app subscription screen, ask why they cancel, attach offers, set colours for light and dark mode, and translate every text, from Lifecycle > Customer Center.
- [Growth insights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/growth-insights.md): Every week RevenueDot AI reads your charts, campaigns and benchmarks and suggests 3 to 5 things to act on, with the numbers behind each one, on the Overview and in an email digest to admins.
- [How do I recover subscribers whose payment failed?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/payment-recovery.md): Payment recovery emails subscribers whose renewal failed on the App Store, Google Play, Amazon or Stripe a link to fix their payment, on a schedule you set, and counts the revenue that comes back.
- [How do I connect my Stripe account without a restricted key?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/stripe-connect.md): Connect with Stripe links your own Stripe account to RevenueDot through Stripe Connect in two clicks. Payments go to your account, RevenueDot takes no fee, and events arrive without a webhook to set up.

## Migrate from RevenueCat

- [Migrate from RevenueCat: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/migrate.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [How do I migrate from RevenueCat to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/migrate/README.md): Import your project with the revenuedot CLI, run both systems side by side with notification forwarding, ship an app update that sets the proxy URL, then cut over. No customer loses access.
- [How do I import a RevenueCat project with the revenuedot CLI?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/migrate/importer.md): revenuedot import copies apps, SDK keys, catalog, customers, subscriptions and purchases from RevenueCat's API v2 into RevenueDot. It resumes after a stop and is safe to run again.
- [How do I run RevenueDot and RevenueCat side by side?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/migrate/dual-run.md): Send store notifications to RevenueDot and let it forward the exact body to RevenueCat, turn on track_new_purchases, keep acting on RevenueCat's webhooks, and compare with revenuedot import verify.
- [What do I change in my app's SDK code to move to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/migrate/sdk-changes.md): In proxy mode, set the proxy URL before configure, turn off signature checks and sync purchases once. With a fork, swap the package and keep your code. Diffs for all ten SDKs.
- [What is the checklist for cutting over from RevenueCat to RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/migrate/cutover-checklist.md): The migration steps in order, from starting the server to turning RevenueCat off, as a checklist. Each step says how to check it is done.
- [What differs between RevenueDot and RevenueCat?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/migrate/what-differs.md): Every known difference as of 2026-10-01, from failed signature checks with the stock SDK to the few SDK calls that answer with a fixed reply and the features still planned, with sources.

## API reference

- [API reference: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/api.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [What APIs does RevenueDot have?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/README.md): RevenueDot serves the SDK endpoints, REST API v1, REST API v2 with extensions, store notification endpoints and webhooks, all described in one OpenAPI 3.1 document.
- [How do I authenticate RevenueDot API requests?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/authentication.md): RevenueDot uses public app keys for the SDK endpoints, secret keys for REST API v1 and v2, and a session cookie for the dashboard. Secret keys carry permissions.
- [What do RevenueDot's API errors mean?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/errors.md): The SDK and REST v1 error codes, the REST v2 error types, which HTTP status each uses, and what to do about each one.
- [Which endpoints do the RevenueCat SDKs call on RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/sdk-endpoints.md): Every SDK endpoint RevenueDot serves, with auth, request fields, error codes and real example responses, plus the store notification endpoints.
- [What can I do with REST API v1?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/rest-v1.md): REST API v1 on RevenueDot: delete customers, grant promotional access, override offerings and run store actions with a secret key.
- [What can I do with REST API v2?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/rest-v2.md): REST API v2 on RevenueDot: projects, apps, products, entitlements, offerings, packages, customers, subscriptions, purchases, metrics and webhooks.
- [Which API endpoints are RevenueDot extensions?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/extensions.md): RevenueDot-only endpoints: dashboard sign-in, OAuth for MCP clients, project settings, store setup, store prices and the product editor, API keys, webhook deliveries, event log, Test Store, web billing, purchase links, funnels, hosted pages, dashboard data and migration import.
- [Which API endpoints does RevenueDot Enterprise add?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/enterprise.md): RevenueDot Enterprise endpoints: licence status, organizations, custom roles and group role mappings, SAML and OpenID Connect single sign-on, SCIM 2.0 provisioning and signed compliance exports.
- [Which webhook events does RevenueDot send?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md): Every webhook event type RevenueDot sends, when each fires, its fields and a real example payload, plus the signature header and retry rules.

## Help center

- [Help center: full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/llms/help.txt): every page of this section in one file
- [Where do I find answers to common RevenueDot problems?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/README.md): The RevenueDot help center, grouped by topic. Each article answers one question, with the fix first.
- [What do people most often ask about RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/faq.md): Short answers about what RevenueDot is, what it costs, its licenses, the stores and SDKs it supports, and what works today.
- [How do I fix common RevenueDot problems?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/troubleshooting.md): A symptom-to-fix list for the SDK, receipts, store notifications, webhooks, the dashboard and self-hosting, with the cause of each.
- [What are the known issues and gaps in RevenueDot?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/known-issues.md): Known issues as of 2026-09-30: what does not work yet, and the workaround for each.
- [Why is my entitlement not active?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/entitlement-not-active.md): Usually the product is not attached to the entitlement, the purchase belongs to another app user ID, the receipt post failed, or the access has ended. Here is how to tell which.
- [What do I do if I forgot my RevenueDot password?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/forgot-password.md): Click Forgot password? on the sign-in page and follow the emailed link within 1 hour. Self-hosted servers without email print the link to the server log, or an admin resets the password from the command line.
- [Why does RevenueDot answer 4xx or 5xx to a receipt?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/receipt-errors-4xx-vs-5xx.md): A 4xx tells the SDK the purchase is permanently bad, so it finishes the transaction for good. A 5xx means try again later, so the SDK keeps the transaction and retries.
- [How do I restore purchases?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/restore-purchases.md): Call restorePurchases from a Restore button, or syncPurchases silently. The project's transfer behaviour decides who owns a purchase another user already has.
- [Why does the SDK report signature verification FAILED in proxy mode?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/signature-verification-failed.md): The stock RevenueCat SDK checks responses against RevenueCat's signing key, which RevenueDot cannot use. Turn verification off, or build the SDK forks with your own key.
- [Why are store notifications not arriving?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/store-notifications-not-arriving.md): Check notification_status in setup health. Most failures are a wrong URL, a bundle ID or package name mismatch, Pub/Sub push auth, or purchases RevenueDot has never seen.
- [How do I test purchases without real money?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/test-sandbox-purchases.md): Use the Test Store for the fastest loop, then App Store sandbox, StoreKit testing in Xcode with the xcode_certificate credential, or Google Play license testers.
- [Why are webhooks not arriving?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/webhooks-not-arriving.md): Check the webhook's delivery log first. Most misses are a filter that excludes the event, a backend that answers something other than 200, or a URL the server cannot reach.
